title: The Stone That Moved

plate.narration: In the Red Sky Foothills, a broad stone stands beside a pale hollow in the grass. The stone is still. The hollow is empty. There is plenty here to look at carefully.

goal.text: Find what moved and get the neighbors safely past the stone.

steps.label: Get the water jars to the keepers
Teach a neighbor the safe road

stone.narration: Three dragonling keepers stare at a stone beside an empty hollow. "Our counting stone moved overnight," says one. "Now the water cart cannot make its turn. Help us find what moved and get the neighbors safely past it." Pip Thistledown, a young manticore Riftseeker, measures the hollow with his tail. A keeper hands him a cord. "Try something that does not twitch."

marks.narration: The stone carries a carved mountain throwing sparks. "An eruption," says a keeper. "Our oldest counts disagree about when it happened." One stroke is chipped. Nobody fills it in. The empty hollow fits the stone, but there are no drag marks between them. Pip writes that down before his tail can add any.

choices.label: Compare the ground and the old drawings

lesson.narration: A kitsune named Seren Wisp is comparing notes with a young manticore named Pip Thistledown. They wear the Riftseekers' clasps. "I am finding what has moved," says Pip. Seren asks you to hum the hall note, then listen for an answering sound. "A starweaver can learn to answer a rift's hum. That is called Attune. No one here chooses a rift's rules."

variants.text: A kitsune named Seren Wisp and a manticore named Pip Thistledown are checking another displaced route. Seren asks you to compare the sounds with what she taught you before. Pip adds the new place to his notes.

footprint.narration: One keeper points from the forked rock. Another checks from the ridge. Their sight lines meet at yesterday's empty hollow. Pip draws a line through the map. "That stone is definitely not where we left it."

grass_test.narration: A gust combs the grass between stone and hollow. When it drops, you can see the pressed blades underneath. Call the quiet moment so a friend can trace the undisturbed strip. A dragged stone should have scraped it. There is no scrape. Pip opens his mouth, then writes "no scrape" instead of guessing what did it.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold when the grass lies still.

onSuccess.narration: The grass between the two places is untouched. Something changed without dragging the stone along that strip.

onFailure.narration: The gust hides your first look. A keeper holds a windbreak while you check again. The grass is untouched; there is no dragged track.

onAssisted.narration: The grass between the two places is untouched. Something changed without dragging the stone along that strip.

views.narration: You lay the road drawing beside the ridge drawing. A rock hidden from the road stands in plain view from the ridge. Both keepers lean in. "Two honest drawings," one says. "One very inconvenient stone." Neither record needs erasing.

witness_result.narration: Together you mark the old hollow and today's stone. The drawings disagree about the view, not about whose work to trust. The eruption date is still uncertain. Wheels squeak on the road: the water cart has arrived. Its owner studies the new turn, then the jars. "Please tell me one of those is the thing you can move back."

cart_plan.narration: "The moved stone blocks the cart's old turn," says a keeper. Keep the jars aboard and build a short ramp around it: you will balance a heavy load, but the cart can use the ramp again. Or leave the cart above the turn and carry the jars along the high path: more passing, less weight near the hollow. The empty cart will still need guiding. Which plan suits your team?

choices.label: Build a reusable ramp for the loaded cart
Pass the jars along the high path
Have our thornguard brace the ramp

ramp_setup.narration: The keeper lays two short boards on sound ground around the turn. Hold them while a friend threads cord beneath the ends. Pip checks the wheel tracks. He starts to draw a proud little flag on the ramp. The cart owner clears her throat. He adds the other wheel track first.

interaction.cue: Hold the ramp while your friend secures the cord.

onSuccess.narration: The ramp stays solid. Now bring the loaded cart across it.

onFailure.narration: The ramp stays solid. Now bring the loaded cart across it.

onAssisted.narration: The ramp stays solid. Now bring the loaded cart across it.

braced_ramp.narration: Your thornguard braces the boards against the sound stones. The cord can be secured without everyone holding a board, so your team skips the extra support job. The cart owner pats a jar. "Your turn to be steady."

cart_balance.narration: Each side of the cart rises or dips as the jars shift. Level it before moving across your ramp. One lid rattles like a tiny bell. The owner walks beside the wheel while Pip keeps his tail firmly out of the spokes. The water belongs in the jars until it reaches the keepers.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side until the loaded cart is level.

onSuccess.narration: The loaded cart rolls over the new ramp. The owner can use this turn again tomorrow.

onFailure.narration: The loaded cart rolls over the new ramp. The owner can use this turn again tomorrow.

onAssisted.narration: The loaded cart rolls over the new ramp. The owner can use this turn again tomorrow.

jar_relay.narration: Pass the sealed water jars along the high path. Each friend catches before passing on; the owner waits at the counting circle to receive them. One keeper calls the order. Pip volunteers to carry two jars at once, looks at his tail, and decides that one is already a full conversation.

interaction.cue: Catch the water jar, then pass it to the next friend.

onSuccess.narration: The jars reach the counting circle without using the fragile turn. You still have an empty cart to bring down.

onFailure.narration: The jars reach the counting circle without using the fragile turn. You still have an empty cart to bring down.

onAssisted.narration: The jars reach the counting circle without using the fragile turn. You still have an empty cart to bring down.

empty_cart.narration: With the jars off, the cart is light enough to turn around the hollow. Guide its front wheel between two sound stones. The owner holds the handles and waits for your call. An empty jar would make an excellent wheel chock, Pip suggests. "It would make an empty jar in pieces," she replies.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold to guide the wheel through the clear gap.

onSuccess.narration: The empty cart reaches the circle. For the next delivery, the jars will need this passing line again.

onFailure.narration: The wheel catches a loose pebble. You stop, move the pebble and guide it through together. The jar-passing route will be needed again.

onAssisted.narration: The empty cart reaches the circle. For the next delivery, the jars will need this passing line again.

water_delivered.narration: Water reaches the counting circle. The keepers fill their cups before returning to the mystery. Pip drinks, counts the cups, and carefully does not count the party. "One more useful thing," says a keeper, nodding at the owner. "A warning, so the next traveler does not trust the old turn."

choices.label: Take a drink and plan the warning

camp.narration: You rest on a low stone while the owner parks the cart. A keeper shares apple slices. Pip uses one to hold his drawing flat, takes a bite, then wonders where his paperweight went. "Two neighbors are due," says a keeper. "A walker from below the blind rise, and a cart from the upper road. Both will need the new turn explained."

choices.label: Help Pip find a better paperweight

paperweight.narration: Pip holds the flapping page with one paw and the remains of his apple with the other. The keepers have seen this before. Each friend can help solve the extremely local problem of keeping a drawing on a rock.

choices.label: Fold the empty edge under the slate
Hold the corner while he finishes

warning.narration: There is one large board for a warning and loose stones for a smaller marker. Put the big sign below the blind rise and walkers will stop in time; your team will need to guide the upper cart. Put it above the turn and carts will have room to brake; your team must meet the walker below. "Both neighbors are coming," Pip reminds you. Which approach should the large sign protect?

choices.label: Warn the walkers below; we will guide the cart
Warn the carts above; we will meet the walker

lower_sign.narration: Carry the large warning down the dry path and pass its cord around the lower posts. From below, the board appears before the hollow. The keeper checks it at a walker's height. Above you, wheels begin to rattle. The smaller marker cannot stop that driver by itself; that is your team's next job.

interaction.cue: Catch and pass the cord around the lower warning posts.

onSuccess.narration: The walker sees the large warning and waits safely below. Your team heads up to guide the approaching cart.

onFailure.narration: The walker sees the large warning and waits safely below. Your team heads up to guide the approaching cart.

onAssisted.narration: The walker sees the large warning and waits safely below. Your team heads up to guide the approaching cart.

upper_sign.narration: Set the board well before the upper turn, leaving room for a cart to stop. Hold it while a friend ties the second corner. The cart driver spots it and brakes. Below the blind rise, a walking neighbor waves at the little stone arrow. She cannot see the hollow from there; you will need to show her.

interaction.cue: Hold the upper sign while your friend ties it.

onSuccess.narration: The cart driver waits above the turn. Your team goes down to meet the walker.

onFailure.narration: The cart driver waits above the turn. Your team goes down to meet the walker.

onAssisted.narration: The cart driver waits above the turn. Your team goes down to meet the walker.

upper_cart.narration: Your big sign is protecting the walker below. Here, the cart driver needs your signal to take the new turn. Wait until the front wheel reaches the keeper's white marker, then call it. Pip holds his tail out as an arrow. It points three different ways. You use your hand instead.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold when the wheel reaches the turning marker.

onSuccess.narration: The driver follows your turn and stops at the circle. The unguarded approach needed your help, just as you planned.

onFailure.narration: You call early. The driver stops while the keeper resets the marker, then follows your clearer signal. Your team has shown where an extra upper warning is needed.

onAssisted.narration: The driver follows your turn and stops at the circle. The unguarded approach needed your help, just as you planned.

lower_neighbor.narration: The cart is safely stopped by your upper sign. Walk the neighbor past the blind rise using the route you actually checked: wait by the forked rock, go around the high side of the hollow, then join the counting circle. Share your landmarks so she can follow without guessing what is behind the rise.

interaction.cue: Give the walker the route from below.
clues: The forked rock is the waiting place before the blind rise.
Go around the hollow after waiting, before joining the keepers.

onSuccess.narration: The neighbor reaches the circle and can repeat the new route. The small lower marker needed your help, as you planned.

onFailure.narration: The neighbor points out a confusing instruction. You walk the checked route with her and correct it. The smaller lower marker still needs an extra warning.

onAssisted.narration: The neighbor reaches the circle and can repeat the new route. The small lower marker needed your help, as you planned.

neighbor_result.narration: Both neighbors are at the counting circle. Your one large sign helped one approach; your team helped the other. The owner marks where another board is needed tomorrow. "Explain the turn back to me," Pip asks the neighbors. They can. Then a thin trickle begins running down the ridge toward the empty hollow.

choices.label: See where the new water is going

variants.text: The lower approach has the big warning. The upper approach still needs a larger sign for carts arriving without your team.
The upper approach has the big warning. Walkers below the blind rise will still need a larger sign of their own.

runoff.narration: The trickle will wash away the sharp edge that helped you measure the hollow. You can aim a small drain into the empty gravel and try to preserve that edge. Or spread loose gravel across the wet patch: a steadier road surface, but the fine footprint will be covered and your drawing must rely on the landmarks you already checked. "Which work should last after you leave?" asks a keeper.

choices.label: Protect the footprint with a small drain
Strengthen the wet road; preserve a simpler drawing

drain.narration: From the dry side, use a narrow board to guide the trickle into the empty gravel. Aim past the hollow's sharp edge. Pip follows the water with his pencil, then remembers pencils are not boats. He catches it just before a tiny voyage begins.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold to guide the trickle past the hollow.

onSuccess.narration: The fine edge stays visible. Your page can include its exact outline.

onFailure.narration: The first trickle washes a corner before you settle the drain. The road stays clear, but your page must leave that fine edge uncertain.

onAssisted.narration: The fine edge stays visible. Your page can include its exact outline.

gravel.narration: Level the shallow gravel tray before spreading its load over the wet patch. The owner tests the new road surface from the dry side. It holds. The fragile outline is now underneath it. "Better wheels," says the keeper. "A simpler drawing. We chose both parts of that."

interaction.cue: Level the gravel tray before spreading the load.

onSuccess.narration: The road surface is steadier. Your record will use the checked landmarks rather than an uncovered fine edge.

onFailure.narration: The road surface is steadier. Your record will use the checked landmarks rather than an uncovered fine edge.

onAssisted.narration: The road surface is steadier. Your record will use the checked landmarks rather than an uncovered fine edge.

evidence_decision.narration: You have the old drawings, today's measurements and whatever the water left visible. Make the traveling page match that evidence. The stone fits its old hollow. The grass has no dragged track. None of this supplies a date for the eruption. Pip leaves the uncertain stroke dotted and offers you the pencil. "Only what we saw," he says.

choices.label: Copy the sharp edge we preserved

exact_copy.narration: You copy the visible outline with the keeper. Even on the precise page, the chipped corner stays dotted. Pip adds a tiny question mark. "Does it need a hat?" The keeper gives him a look that answers a different question.

landmark_copy.narration: The keeper records the forked rock, old hollow and today's stone. The washed or covered fine edge stays blank. She writes "from the road" above the drawing. The next keeper will know where you stood, even where you could not measure.

motion.narration: Beside the stone, a fold in the air is narrowing. Seren holds two fingers apart, then brings them closer. "We should show late travelers what that means." You can copy its changing width, or a starweaver can use a skill called Attune to compare its hum. Nobody needs to cross it to learn that its remaining time is shrinking.

choices.label: Have our starweaver compare its changing hum

motion_memory.narration: Pip marks the fold's width each time Seren taps the slate. For two taps it stays wide; then it narrows, then narrows again. Watch and copy that pattern. A keeper lays a little cord circle beside the marks. "This is the waiting place. It is not an invitation to jump."

interaction.cue: Watch the width marks, then copy the change.

onSuccess.narration: Your marks show time running out, not where the opening goes.

onFailure.narration: Seren repeats the observations slowly and you correct the marks. The opening is shrinking; the destination remains unknown.

onAssisted.narration: Your marks show time running out, not where the opening goes.

motion_attuned.narration: Your starweaver answers the fold's hum with Attune while the party watches its edges. The steady answering note gives you a wider target for matching the next pulse. A friend can make the call. The sound helps with timing; it does not change the opening's rules.

interaction.cue: Use the answering note to match the pulse in the wider gold band.

onSuccess.narration: The answered pulse and the visible narrowing agree. The opening is running out of time.

onFailure.narration: You miss one pulse. Seren helps you compare the next with its edges. It is still narrowing; the answer does not change its rules.

onAssisted.narration: The answered pulse and the visible narrowing agree. The opening is running out of time.

stone_priority.narration: "I can give one drawing the biggest space on my traveling page," says Pip. A road plan will be useful at the next changed crossing; an old-mark drawing preserves the uncertain count for comparison with another stone. The keepers retain both full records here. Choose which work your party will finish and carry forward first.

route_copy.narration: The cart owner keeps the local road plan for tomorrow's delivery. Pip checks the traveling copy with you and slides it into his notebook. "Next time the road argues with the map, we have a starting point."

carving_copy.narration: The keeper copies the long stroke, short strokes and uncertain chip. The chip stays a question. The eruption still has no agreed date. Pip draws a dotted box beside the marks. "For the bit we do not know. Might need a bigger notebook."

rest.narration: The water jars stand beside full cups. The old hollow and today's stone are recorded, with no invented eruption date. Both neighbors can explain the new turn. Pip packs the traveling page. "Thank you, team," he says. The road to Ashspan Bridge is open. The narrowing fold is another possible way onward; if you take the road instead, its remaining chance will pass.

variants.text: Your large sign warns walkers below the rise. The keepers will add a larger upper sign for the next carts.
Your large sign stops carts above the turn. The keepers will add a larger lower warning for walkers.
The reusable ramp remains for tomorrow's water delivery.
Tomorrow's jars will need the high-path passing line again; the cart route has not become a loaded ramp.
The original fine edge remains available for another measurement.
The fine edge is no longer clear. The checked landmarks remain on the page; the missing detail stays missing.

paperweight_response_rock.narration: Pip puts the pebble on the corner. "A paperweight that does not become lunch. Excellent." With the drawing safely weighted, you can deal with the actual road.

paperweight_response_fold.narration: The page stays flat. Pip gives the folded corner a suspicious look, then nods. With the drawing safely weighted, you can deal with the actual road.

paperweight_response_hold.narration: Pip finishes the line and thanks you. His tail tries to help. You move it off the ink. With the drawing safely weighted, you can deal with the actual road.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
